# Baxi ASHP Control: controller navigation reference

Built 2026-10-24 from *Baxi ASHP Control installation, user and service
manual* (7887625 v04), cite as "Baxi ASHP Control IM, p.N". This is the
lookup the assistant uses to give installers button-by-button steps on the
Baxi user interface (MK2.2) on the indoor control unit used with the
Assure HP55 outdoor unit.

**Keep it separate from Panasonic.** Different buttons, menus and access.
Never use a Panasonic step, menu name or key combination on a Baxi, or the
reverse.

**Buttons confirmed (Donal, 2026-10-24)** from the manual's Fig.11 on p.15
(image saved at `manuals/baxi/originals/baxi-ashp-control-fig11-p15-buttons.png`):
three controls under the display. The manual text file lost the button icons
inside sentences ("1. Press the  button."), but the figure, the carousel text
on p.17 ("Display the carousel by pressing the Main menu button", "Scroll
through the menu by turning the button") and Donal's confirmation that the
centre knob scrolls to the options on screen settle the steps below. Two
Clearing the error memory was confirmed by Donal from the p.134 page image
(saved in originals/): press and hold the [Dial]. The child lock override
was confirmed from the 12.1 page image (p.106, saved in originals/): briefly
press [Menu] and [Dial] together. All button steps are now covered.

---

## C1. Buttons and screens (Fig.11, p.15)

Layout under the display, left to right: **[Back]**, **[Dial]**, **[Menu]**.

| Answer name | Manual label (p.15) | Where / symbol | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Back]** | 1 Back button | Small round button, left; curved back arrow ↩ | Back to the previous screen |
| **[Menu]** | 2 Main menu button | Small round button, right; three lines in a circle ☰ | Opens the carousel (main menu) |
| **[Dial]** turn | 4 Selection/validation button | Large rotary knob, centre; dot in a circle ⊙ | Turn to scroll through items or change a value |
| **[Dial]** press | 4 Selection/validation button | Press the centre knob | Select / confirm |

Display backlight (Tab.5, p.15): **blue** = normal operation; **continuous
red** = warning or blockage; **flashing red** = lockout. Standby after 5 min
with no button pressed; press any button to wake it (p.15). Turning the dial
on the home screen steps through the zone screens (p.16).

Menu paths in the manual are written " > Installer > ..." with the leading
icon lost. They start from the carousel, so every path starts with **[Menu]**.

**Installer level (p.41):** [Menu], select **Installer**, enter code
**0012**. All installer functions open. It times out after 30 min with no
action. The unit does **not** need to be switched off first (that rule is
Panasonic only). The "Installer level activated" icon shows on screen (p.16).

## C2. Carousel menus (Tab.8, p.17)

Operating mode · Domestic Hot Water On/Off · Heating temperature · Water
temperature · Temporary heating temperature change · Hot water boost ·
System holiday mode · User settings · Test mode · **Installer** (code) ·
**Finder** (parameter search, installer) · **Signals overview** (measured
values, installer) · Energy overview · System settings · Version information.
Menus shown depend on the system configuration.

Installer menu branches used in the manual: Installation setup (Heat Pump,
Zone1, Zone3, Zone2, Domestic Hot Water, Mixed/circul. DHW, Outdoor
temperature, Solar systems), Signals, Counters, Error history,
Commissioning > Test mode, Advanced menu (Set configuration code, Auto
detect, Reset to factory settings).

## C5. Start and stop (p.122)

Start: switch on the outdoor unit and the indoor unit (auto vent about
3 min), then any backup boiler. Shut down: switch off heating/cooling,
outdoor unit power, indoor unit power, backup boiler. For long absences use
System holiday mode instead of switching off (frost protection and pump
anti-seize keep running). After a fault: off, wait 3 min, then indoor unit
on first, then outdoor unit (p.124, p.129).

The system is shut down but automatically switches on again when the error disappears.

ctlFaults.checks: BL input on the central unit PCB terminal block open: Check the contact on the BL input. Check the wiring. Check parameters AP001 and AP100.

Flow rate sensor: Check the electrical connections and the direction of the flow meter (arrow to the right). Replace the flow meter if necessary.

ctlFaults.checks: The system's refrigerant level is too low. Add the appropriate quantity. In heating or DHW mode, the outdoor heat exchanger is dirty or clogged. Clean the exchanger. The water flow rate is too low in cooling mode. Increase the water flow rate.

ctlFaults.meaning: DeltaT CH max limit The Delta Temperature on the central heating side exceeds the maximum overshoot.
ctlFaults.checks: Check whether the water filter needs cleaning. Make sure that there is no air in the system (venting). Check the water pressure. The water pressure must be above 1 bar (0.1 MPa) (at low temperature). Check that the pump's speed setting is the highest speed. Make sure that the expansion vessel is not broken. Check that the resistance in the hydraulic circuit is not too high for the pump.

ctlFaults.checks: Check the wiring between the EHC–16 PCB and the sensor. Check that the sensor has been fitted properly. Check the Ohmic value of the sensor. Replace the sensor if necessary.

ctlFaults.meaning: Heating error Heating operation error
Refr pressure Refrigerant pressure sensor error
ctlFaults.checks: Check the wiring between the EHC–16 PCB and the sensor. Check that the sensor has been fitted correctly. Reconnect the sensor connector, if necessary. Check the ohmic value of the sensor. Replace the sensor if necessary.

The electric expansion valve is locked or the winding connector is loose. Tap the valve body and connect/disconnect the connector several times to check that the valve is working correctly. Fit the winding in the correct position. DHW mode: the water tank's heat exchanger is smaller. Cooling mode: The heat exchanger cover has not been taken off: remove the cover The heat exchanger is dirty or clogged. Clean the heat exchanger.

ctlFaults.checks: Check the wiring between the EHC–16 PCB and the sensor. Check that the sensor has been fitted properly. Check the Ohmic value of the sensor. Replace the sensor if necessary.

ctlFaults.checks: Check the wiring between the EHC–16 PCB and the sensor. Check that the sensor has been fitted properly. Check the Ohmic value of the sensor. Replace the sensor if necessary.

Comm IDU - ODU Communication error between the indoor unit and outdoor unit
ctlFaults.checks: The main PCB B and the main control PCB of the hydraulic module are not connected. Connect the wire. Check the value of signal HM024. If the value of HM024 is less than 75%, the communication errors are too severe. It is essential to use a shielded communication cable. If there is a strong magnetic field or strong interference, (e.g. lifts, powerful transformers), add a barrier to protect the unit or move the unit to another location. 1. Switch off the outdoor unit and the indoor unit. 2. Wait 3 minutes for the outdoor unit capacitors to discharge. 3. Switch on the indoor unit then the outdoor unit.

ctlFaults.meaning: ODU power module Outdoor unit power module is anomalous
ctlFaults.checks: The power supply voltage of the unit is low, increase the power supply voltage to the required range. The space between the units is too narrow for heat exchange. Increase the space between the units. The heat exchanger is dirty or clogged. Clean the exchanger. The fan is not running. The fan motor or the fan is broken. Replace it. The refrigerant level is too high. Adjust the quantity of refrigerant. The water flow rate is low, there is air in the system or the pump stroke is insufficient. Release the air and reselect the pump. The water outlet temperature sensor has come loose or is broken; reconnect or replace it. The wires or screws on the module are loose. Reconnect the wires and tighten the screws. The thermally conductive adhesive has dried out or has fallen off. Add a little thermally conductive adhesive. The wire connection is loose or has fallen off. Reconnect the wire. The inverter module board is faulty, replace it. If you find that there is no problem with the control system, then the compressor is faulty, replace it with a new one. The isolation valves are closed, open them.

ctlFaults.meaning: ODU superheat The outdoor unit superheat is anomalous
Fan motor Outdoor unit fan motor is anomalous.
ctlFaults.checks: A strong wind is blowing against the fan, making it turn in the opposite direction. Reorient the unit or shelter it to prevent the wind from blowing against the fan. The fan motor is broken, replace it.

ctlFaults.meaning: Overheat protection The outdoor unit overheat protection is activated
ODU pressure The outdoor unit pressure is anomalous
ODU overcurrent Compressor overcurrent in the outdoor unit
ctlFaults.checks: See possible causes and action list for code H06.24. The power supply voltage of the unit is low. Increase the power voltage to the required range.

ctlFaults.meaning: ODU current sensor Current sensor error in the outdoor unit
ODU Tinl water The outdoor unit inlet water temperature is anomalous
ODU refrigerant Outdoor unit refrigerant is anomalous
DIP switch The DIP switch on the interface board has a configuration error
ctlFaults.checks: interface panel = EHC–16 PCB

ctlFaults.meaning: Tambiant air minimum The ambient air temperature is below the allowed minimum
HP outdoor temp Heat pump outdoor temperature sensor error
HP suction temp Heat pump compressor suction temperature sensor error
ctlFaults.checks: The connector of sensor Th is loose. Reconnect it. The connector of temperature sensor Th is wet or contains water. Drain the water, dry the connector and add waterproof adhesive. The temperature sensor Th is faulty. Replace it.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP inverter voltage The inverter voltage of the heat pump is too low
ctlFaults.checks: Check the power supply. If the power supply is correct, check that the LED indicator light is ok. Check the PN voltage: if it is 380 V, the source of the problem is generally the motherboard. If the indicator light is off, switch off the power supply, check the IGBT, check the dioxides, if the voltage is not correct, the inverter board is damaged, replace it. If there is no problem with the IGBT, this means that there are no problems with the inverter board. Check the bridge rectifier to see if the bridge voltage is correct. (Same method as for the IGBT, disconnect the power supply, check if the dioxides are damaged. normally, if F1 is present when the compressor is started up, the motherboard could be the problem. If F1 is present when the fan is started up, this could be due to the inverter board.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP supply voltage The heat pump power supply voltage is out of range
ctlFaults.checks: Check that the power supply input is in the available range. Switch off and on again several times in quick succession. The unit should remain off for more than 3 minutes before being switched back on. The part in the circuit on the main control board is faulty. Replace it with a new main PCB.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP discharge temp Heat pump compressor discharge temperature sensor error
ctlFaults.checks: See possible causes and action list for code H06.24. The temperature sensor TWout is loose. Reconnect it. The temperature sensor T1 is loose. Reconnect it. The temperature sensor T5 is loose. Reconnect it.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP EEPROM error Heat pump Inverter module EEPROM error
ctlFaults.checks: Error in the EEprom parameter, rewrite EEprom data. The part in the EEprom chip is broken, replace it. The main PCB is broken, replace it.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP inverter com Communication error between the outdoor main control unit and the inverter module of
ctlFaults.checks: the heat pump If there is a power supply connected to the PCB and to the drive board. Check whether the PCB LED is on or off. If the LED is off, reconnect the power supply wire. If the LED is on, check the wire connection between the main PCB and the drive PCB. If the wire is loose or broken, reconnect the wire or replace it. Fit a new main PCB or drive board.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP high temp cooling HP refrigerant outlet temperature is too high in cooling mode
ctlFaults.checks: The heat exchanger cover has not been taken off. Remove it. The heat exchanger is dirty or clogged. Clean the exchanger. There is insufficient space around the unit for heat exchange. The fan motor is broken, replace it.

ctlFaults.meaning: HP gas temp Heat pump gas temperature sensor error
ctlFaults.checks: Check the sensor resistance The connector for sensor T2B is loose. Reconnect it. The connector for sensor T2B is wet or contains water. Drain the water and dry the connector. Add a waterproof adhesive. Sensor T2B is faulty, replace it with a new sensor.

ctlFaults.meaning: ODU return high flow The heat pump return temperature is higher than the flow temperature in the outdoor
ctlFaults.checks: unit Check the resistance of the two Tw_out - Tw_in sensors Check the position of the two sensors. The water inlet/outlet sensor (TWJn/TW_out) is broken, replace it with a new sensor. The 4-way valve is jammed. Restart the unit again to allow the valve to change the direction. The 4-way valve is broken, replace it with a new valve.

ctlFaults.checks: unit The connector for sensor T3 is loose. Reconnect it. The connector for sensor T3 is wet or contains water. Drain the water and dry the connector. Add a waterproof adhesive. Sensor T3 is faulty, replace it with a new sensor.

ctlFaults.meaning: 3 phase sequence Invalid phase sequence in the 3 phase heat pump power supply
ctlFaults.checks: Check that the power supply cables are correctly connected and avoid phase loss. Check whether the connections of the neutral and live wires have been reversed.

ctlFaults.meaning: ODU flow error Water flow error active in the outdoor unit module
ctlFaults.checks: Check whether the water filter needs cleaning. Make sure that there is no air in the system (venting). Check the water pressure. The water pressure must be greater than 1 bar (0.1 MPa). Check that the pump's speed setting is the highest speed. Make sure that the expansion vessel is not broken. Check that the resistance in the hydraulic circuit is not too high for the pump. If this error occurs during operation in Defrost mode (when heating spaces or domestic water), make sure that the power supply to the backup electric heater is correctly cabled and the fuses are not blown. Check that the pump fuse and the PCB fuse are not blown. The electric circuit is short circuited or open. Reconnect the wire correctly. The water flow rate is too low. The water flow rate controller is faulty, it is continuously open or closed. Switch the water flow rate controller.

ctlFaults.checks: Check the sensor resistance The connector for the Tw_in sensor is loose. Reconnect it. The connector for the Tw_in sensor is wet or contains water. Drain the water and dry the connector. Add a waterproof adhesive The Tw_in sensor is faulty. Replace it with a new sensor.

ctlFaults.checks: The EEprom parameter is incorrect. Rewrite the EEprom data. The EEprom chip is broken. Replace it with a new EEprom chip. The main control PCB for the hydraulic module is broken. Replace it with a new PCB.

ctlFaults.checks: boards The cable is not connecting the main PCB B and the main control PCB of the hydraulic module. Connect the cable. The communication cable order is incorrect. # Panasonic wired remote controller: navigation reference

Built 2026-10-23 from the two Panasonic manuals on file. This is the lookup
the assistant uses to give installers button-by-button steps on the wired
remote controller (the panel on the unit or wall, not a phone app).

- **Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32** (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5). Source:
  *Panasonic Service Manual, Mini Monobloc R32 J-series* (cite as "J-series
  SM, p.N"). The text came from the PDF's text layer, and most button icons
  inside sentences were lost ("Press  for 5 sec."). The original PDF arrived
  on 2026-10-24 (`manuals/panasonic/originals/Panasonic-J-series-Mini-Monobloc-R32-Service-Manual.pdf`),
  and the hidden-menu key combinations and error-history clearing (A4) were
  read from its page images.
- **Part B: K-series split Hydromodule + Tank** (WH-ADC0309K3E5/K3E5AN/K6E5/
  K6E5AN, outdoor WH-UDZ03/05/07/09KE5). Source: *Panasonic Installation
  Manual, Hydromodule + Tank K-series* (cite as "K-series IM, p.N"). Button
  steps here were read from the original PDF page images (pp.21-34), so the
  icons are known.
- **Part C: J-series T-Cap monobloc R32** (WH-MXC09J3E5 / WH-MXC12J6E5).
  Source: *Panasonic Service Manual, Monobloc T-Cap J-series 9 and 12 kW*,
  Order No PAPAMY2101001CE (cite as "T-Cap SM, p.N"). Added 26/10/2026. Its
  controller pages match the J-series Mini Monobloc, so Part C is Part A with
  the T-Cap page numbers, checked against the T-Cap manual and its page images.
- **Part D: L-series R290 Hydromodule + Tank** (tank unit WH-ADC0509L3E51,
  outdoor WH-WDG05LE5 / WDG07LE5 / WDG09LE5). Source: *Panasonic Service
  Manual, Hydromodule + Tank R290 L-series*, Order No PCZ2504005CE (cite as
  "L-series SM, p.N"). Added 26/10/2026. Its menu pages (pp.37-67) have no
  text layer, so they were read by OCR and the key combinations were read
  from the page images (pp.123, 222-226, 235-236).

**Keep the parts separate.** The manuals show the same button layout, but
menu lists, item numbers and hidden-menu key combinations are documented
separately. Never use a Part B key combination or menu item for a J-series
unit, or the reverse, and give T-Cap page numbers (Part C) for a T-Cap and L-series page numbers (Part D) for an L-series. If something is only in one part, say it is not
covered for the other model.

---

## Button names used in answers

Both manuals label the controller buttons A to G (J-series SM p.74, K-series
IM p.21). Use these names in every answer:

| Answer name | Manual label | Symbol on the button | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[Menu]** | B: Menu | ☰ (three lines) | Open/close the main menu |
| **[▲] [▼] [◄] [►]** | C: Triangle (Move) | arrow keys | Select or change an item |
| **[OK]** | G: OK | ↵ (return arrow) | Confirm |
| **[Back]** | E: Back | ↩ (curved arrow) | Back to previous item |
| **[Quick Menu]** | F: Quick Menu | ⠿ (grid of dots) | Open/close the quick menu |
| **[Operate]** | D: Operate | ⏻ (power symbol, with LED) | Start/stop operation |

Layout on the panel (K-series IM p.21): top row Back, ▲, Menu; middle row ◄,
OK, ►; bottom row Quick Menu, ▼, Operate. Every list screen shows "Select"
(arrows) and "[↵] Confirm" in its footer.

---

# Part A: J-series Mini Monobloc R32

## A1. First power-up (J-series SM p.22, p.75)

1. Initialising screen shows for about 10 s, then the normal screen.
2. Press any button: the Language screen opens. [▲]/[▼] to choose, [OK].
3. Clock format 24h or am/pm: [▲]/[▼], [OK].
4. Date & time: arrows to set year/month/day/hour/min, [OK].
5. Back at the start screen. Press [Menu], select Installer setup.

If this initial setting is not done, the controller will not go into the
menus (p.75).

## A2. Main menu tree (J-series SM pp.23-36, p.75)

[Menu] opens Main Menu. Items 1-4 are user menus, 5-7 installer.
J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting."

- **Function setup**: Weekly timer, Holiday timer, Quiet timer, Room heater,
  Tank heater, Sterilization (p.23)
- **System check**: Energy monitor, System information, Error history,
  Compressor, Heater (p.24)
- **Personal setup**: Touch sound, LCD contrast, Backlight, Backlight
  intensity, Clock format, Date & Time, Language, Unlock password (4 digits,
  default 0000) (pp.24-25)
- **Service contact**: Contact 1 / Contact 2 (p.25)
- **Installer setup** (pp.26-36, flow chart pp.76-77)
  - **System setup**, in this order: Optional PCB connectivity, Zone &
    Sensor, Heater capacity, Anti freezing, Tank connection, DHW capacity,
    Buffer tank connection*, Tank heater (only if Tank connection = Yes),
    Base pan heater, Alternative outdoor sensor, Bivalent connection,
    External SW, Solar connection*, External error signal*, Demand
    control*, SG ready*, External compressor SW*, Circulation liquid,
    Heat-Cool SW*, Force heater, Force defrost, Defrost signal, Pump
    flowrate. (*Only shown when Optional PCB connectivity = Yes; optional
    PCB is CZ-NS4P, p.66.)
  - **Operation setup**: Heat, Cool (cooling unlocked only), Auto (cooling
    unlocked only), Tank (only if Tank connection = Yes)
  - **Service setup**: Pump maximum speed, Pump down, Dry concrete, Service
    contact

## A3. Step-by-step recipes (J-series)

General path into any installer item:
0. **Turn the heat pump OFF first:** press [Operate] (⏻) so the operation LED goes out. Installer setup can't be opened while the unit is running (J-series SM p.23: "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting"; confirmed on site by Donal, HMG Field Notes 2026-10-23). Remind the installer to switch it back on with [Operate] when finished.
1. [Menu] (top-right button)
2. [▼] to **Installer setup**, [OK]
3. [▲]/[▼] to System setup / Operation setup / Service setup, [OK]
4. [▲]/[▼] to the item, [OK]
5. [▲]/[▼] (or [◄]/[►] on multi-field screens) to change, [OK] to store
6. [Back] to step out, [Menu] to close

**Check it changed:** open the item again and read the value back. Where a
setting has a visible effect, it is listed below.

| Task | Path after "Installer setup" | Options / default | Check it changed | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| External room thermostat (or internal, room thermistor, water temp) | System setup → Zone & Sensor | Without optional PCB: Water temperature / Room thermostat (Internal or External) / Room thermistor. Default "Room and Water temp." | Main screen sensor-type icon changes (p.21 lists Water temperature, Compensation curve, Direct, Room thermostat External, Room thermostat Internal, Room thermistor icons) | pp.26, 78; wiring examples pp.64-65 |
| 2-zone / pool | System setup → Optional PCB connectivity = Yes, then Zone & Sensor → 1 or 2 zone | Pool only on zone 2 | Zone 1 / Zone 2 appear in Operation setup | pp.26, 78 |
| Backup heater capacity | System setup → Heater capacity | 3 / 6 / 9 kW depending on model | Re-open item | pp.26, 78 |
| Anti freezing | System setup → Anti freezing | Yes (default) / No | Re-open item | pp.26, 78 |
| Tank connected | System setup → Tank connection | No (default) / Yes | Tank temp appears on main screen; Operation setup shows Tank | pp.26, 78 |
| Tank heater internal/external | System setup → Tank heater | Internal (default) / External + ON time 0:20 | Re-open item. Also set Function setup → Tank heater ON to use it (p.79) | pp.27, 79 |
| Bivalent (boiler) | System setup → Bivalent connection → Yes → Auto or SG ready → pattern | Alternative / Parallel / Advanced parallel; ON temp -5 °C default | Boiler icon on main screen (p.80) | pp.27-29, 80 |
| Glycol | System setup → Circulation liquid | Water (default) / Glycol | Re-open item | pp.30, 82 |
| Pump control mode | System setup → Pump flowrate | ΔT (default) / Max. duty | Re-open item | pp.31, 82 |
| Heating curve or fixed flow temp | Operation setup → Heat → Water temp. for heating ON → Compensation curve or Direct | Curve default: -5 °C → 55 °C, 15 °C → 35 °C. Direct default 35 °C. Range 20-60 °C. HMG recommends: steel rads -3 °C → 45 °C, 15 °C → 35 °C; UFH -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C; HMG max flow 45 °C rads, 35 °C UFH (HMG weather compensation guidance) | Main screen temp-setting icon (curve vs direct), re-open item | pp.31-32, 83 |

| Pump maximum speed, read flow rate, air purge | Service setup → Pump maximum speed | Screen shows Flow rate (0.1-99.9 L/min), Max. Duty (range 0x40-0xFF, 0xCE example), Operation (OFF / ON / Air Purge). [▲]/[▼] sets Max. Duty, [►] moves to Operation, [▲]/[▼] picks OFF/ON/Air Purge, [◄] goes back. [Operate] turns the pump off on either screen | Flow rate reading on the same screen; also System check → System information → Pump flowrate | pp.35, 84, 151-152 |
| Pump down | Service setup → [OK] → [▼] to Pump down → [OK] → ON → [OK]. [Back] cancels | Screen shows "Pump down operation in progress!"; press [Operate] to stop, screen returns to "[⏻] Start" | Message on screen | pp.36, 84, 150 |
| Screed drying | Service setup → Dry concrete → Edit → [OK]: set number of stages (1-99, [▲]/[▼], [OK]), then each stage's water temp (25-55 °C, 1 °C steps, [OK] per stage; [Back] returns to the previous stage). After the last stage it returns to the ON/Edit screen. Select ON → [OK] to start | Status screen shows Stage n/N, water set temp and actual temp; stage moves on each day. [Operate] stops it | Re-open item | pp.36, 84, 155-156 |
| Installer phone number | Service setup → Service contact → Contact 1/2 | Name and number | Personal menu → Service contact | pp.36, 84 |

User-menu recipes (no Installer setup needed):

| Task | Steps | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Error history | [Menu] → [▲]/[▼] to System check → [OK] → Error history → [OK]. Shows the last 4 errors, most recent at top | pp.24, 163 |
| Live readings (inlet, outlet, zones, tank, buffer, solar, pool, compressor frequency, pump flowrate) | [Menu] → System check → System information → [OK] | p.24 |
| Energy / COP | [Menu] → System check → Energy monitor | p.24 |
| Quick menu items | [Quick Menu] → [▲]/[▼] to select → [OK] to turn on/off. Items: Force DHW, Powerful, Quiet, Force Heater, Weekly Timer, Force Defrost, Error Reset, R/C Lock | p.22 |
| Clear a displayed error | [Quick Menu] → Error Reset. On the error screen itself, select Close / Reset and confirm. If the fault is still there, it returns | pp.22, 162 |
| Weekly timer / holiday / quiet timer | [Menu] → Function setup → item | p.23 |
| Language, clock, contrast | [Menu] → Personal setup → item | pp.24-25 |

**Clear error history permanently (p.163):** [Menu] → System check → [OK] →

steps.title: Pipework and wiring finished
steps.text: All water pipework and electrical cable connections are properly done before filling or test run (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Pipe duct sealed and dry
steps.text: The duct carrying the flow and return pipes between the outdoor and indoor unit is sealed and has no water in it. A wet duct makes the unit run constantly and trip on F12 (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).

steps.title: Cylinder sensor in place
steps.text: If there is a DHW cylinder: the cylinder sensor is fully in the sensor pocket at the correct position, so it reads the real cylinder temperature. A misplaced sensor causes F12 trips (HMG Field Notes – F12 high pressure trips on site).

steps.title: Fill and purge the water circuit
steps.text: Remove the cover (2 screws). Turn the air purge valve plug anticlockwise one full turn. Set the pressure relief valve lever DOWN. Fill at more than 1 bar through the water inlet until water flows freely from the pressure relief valve drain hose (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Water only, no glycol
steps.text: HMG recommends water only in the circuit (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Set Circulation liquid to Water in stage 3, and keep Anti freezing on Yes. Note: the manual itself recommends 40% propylene glycol (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Expansion vessel big enough
steps.text: Built-in vessel is 6 L at 1 bar pre-charge, good for up to 150 L of system water without antifreeze. Over 150 L, or with glycol, add a vessel. If the highest point is more than 7 m above the unit, set the pre-charge to (height in m × 10 + 30) kPa (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Water pressure
steps.text: With all power off, fill to **1 to 1.5 bar** on the unit's water pressure gauge (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Never lower than 0.05 MPa (0.5 bar) (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Pressure relief valve tested
steps.text: Turn the lever horizontal and listen for the clack of water draining, then push the lever back down. If water keeps draining, switch off and escalate (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Power on, pump running, no leaks
steps.text: Switch on the supply and check the water pump runs and there are no leaks at the pipe connections. Refit the cover (J-series SM p.62).

steps.title: RCCB tested
steps.text: With power on, press TEST on the RCCB: the lever drops to 0. Touch nothing else inside. Set the lever back ON (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Language, clock and date set
steps.text: About 10 s after power-up, press any button: choose the language, clock format (24h) and date and time, [OK] after each. The controller won't open the menus until this is done (J-series SM p.22, p.75).

steps.title: Get into Installer setup
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ so the operation light goes out, then [Menu] (top right) › Installer setup › System setup. Installer setup is locked while the unit runs (J-series SM p.23; HMG Field Notes – Can't get into Installer setup).

steps.title: Optional PCB connectivity
steps.text: Yes only if the optional PCB (CZ-NS4P) is fitted, e.g. for 2 zones, solar or SG ready. Otherwise leave No (J-series SM p.26, p.66).

steps.title: Zone & Sensor
steps.text: HMG: **Room thermostat, External**, with the weather compensation curve (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Options are Water temperature, Room thermostat (Internal or External) or Room thermistor; 1 or 2 zones with the optional PCB (J-series SM p.26, p.78).

steps.title: Heater capacity
steps.text: HMG: **3 kW** backup heater on the 5, 7 and 9 kW models (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Options 3, 6 or 9 kW depending on model (J-series SM p.26, p.78).

steps.title: Anti freezing
steps.text: HMG: **Yes** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (J-series SM p.26).

steps.title: Tank connection and tank heater
steps.text: If a DHW cylinder is fitted: Tank connection = Yes, then Tank heater = Internal or External (factory Internal, ON time 0:20). To use the tank heater also set Function setup › Tank heater ON (J-series SM pp.26-27, p.79).

steps.title: Bivalent connection
steps.text: Only if a boiler is connected: Yes › Auto or SG ready › pattern (Alternative, Parallel, Advanced parallel). Otherwise leave No (J-series SM pp.27-29, p.80).

steps.title: Circulation liquid
steps.text: Water or Glycol, to match what's in the system (J-series SM p.30, p.82).

steps.title: Pump flowrate
steps.text: HMG: **ΔT** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Other option Max. duty (J-series SM p.31, p.82).

steps.title: Heating curve (HMG)
steps.text: Operation setup › Heat › Water temp. for heating ON › Compensation curve. HMG: steel radiators -3 °C outdoor → 45 °C flow, 15 °C → 35 °C. Underfloor -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C. The factory curve (-5 °C → 55 °C) is over the HMG maximum, so always change it. On 2 zones set Zone 1 and Zone 2 (HMG weather compensation guidance; J-series SM pp.31-32, p.83).

steps.title: Maximum flow (HMG)
steps.text: Never above 45 °C on radiators or 35 °C on underfloor. On the Panasonic the -3 °C curve point is the maximum: there is no separate maximum flow setting in the manual (HMG weather compensation guidance).

steps.title: Outdoor temp. for heating OFF
steps.text: HMG: **24 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 5-35 °C (J-series SM p.32, p.83).

steps.title: ΔT for heating ON
steps.text: HMG: **5 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 1-15 °C (J-series SM p.32, p.83).

steps.title: Heater ON/OFF
steps.text: HMG: outdoor temp for heater ON **-3 °C** (factory 0 °C) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave the rest at factory: delay 30 min, heater ON at 4 °C below target water temperature, OFF at 2 °C below (J-series SM pp.32-33, p.83).

steps.title: Tank timings
steps.text: HMG: Tank re-heat temp **-8 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave Floor operation time (8:00) and Tank heat up time (1:00) at factory (J-series SM pp.34-35, p.84).

steps.title: Sterilization (legionella)
steps.text: HMG: **65 °C for 10 min** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Operation setup › Tank › Sterilization. Set the day and time to suit the customer in Function setup › Sterilization (J-series SM pp.23, 34-35, p.84).

steps.title: Air purge
steps.text: Service setup › Pump maximum speed › [►] to Operation › [▲]/[▼] to Air Purge › [OK]. Run it until the flow reading is steady. [Operate] stops the pump (J-series SM p.35, pp.151-152).

steps.title: Flow rate checked
steps.text: Read Flow rate on the same screen. Must be at least 15 l/min with the main pump running; low flow can cause H75 during defrost (J-series SM p.63). Nominal flow: 5 kW 14.3, 7 kW 20, 9 kW 25.8 l/min (HMG sizing guidance; J-series SM p.12). HMG: leave pump Max. Duty at the factory setting, adjusting only if the site needs it (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: Service contact
steps.text: Service setup › Service contact › Contact 1: HMG: **Heat Merchants Technical Support** (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (J-series SM p.36). No phone number needed.

steps.title: Screed drying
steps.text: Only on a new screed floor: Service setup › Dry concrete › Edit, set stages and temperatures (25-55 °C), then ON. Follow the screed maker's schedule (J-series SM p.36, pp.155-156).

steps.title: Start the unit
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ to switch back on and run heating (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: Pressure while running
steps.text: Gauge reads between 0.05 and 0.3 MPa (0.5 to 3 bar) (J-series SM p.63).

steps.title: No leaks
steps.text: Check every water connection for leaks during the test run (J-series SM p.53).

steps.text: With the heating running and every zone valve open, read the flow: [Menu] › System check › System information › Pump flowrate. It should be at least 15 l/min and close to the unit's nominal flow from stage 6 (J-series SM p.24, p.63; HMG commissioning check, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.text: Close every zone so all the flow goes through the bypass valve. Read the flow again in the same way, and adjust the bypass valve until it reaches the unit's nominal flow rate from stage 6 (HMG: nominal flow across the bypass, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.text: Show the customer how to use the controller and how to look after the unit (J-series SM p.4).

steps.title: Unit left running
steps.text: Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.

steps.title: Tank unit and pipework checked
steps.text: Tank unit properly installed on a concrete floor, no gas leak at the flare nuts, flare nut connections insulated, water drainage properly done (K-series IM p.12 checklist).

steps.text: Refrigerant pipework, leak test and evacuation by an F-Gas certified installer. R32 is mildly flammable (A2L). The outdoor unit manual isn't on file, so the app has no step-by-step for this.

steps.title: RCCB/ELCB tested
steps.text: With power on, test the RCCB/ELCB and set it back ON (K-series IM pp.10-11).

steps.text: In winter, leave the unit powered on standby for at least 15 minutes before the test run, so the refrigerant warms up and no wrong error code shows (K-series IM p.12).

steps.title: Unit left running
steps.text: Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.

steps.title: Pipework and wiring finished
steps.text: Pipework and electrical cable connections properly done, tank unit filled with water and trapped air released, before the test run (L-series SM p.93).

steps.title: R290 outdoor unit sited safely
steps.text: The outdoor unit holds R290, which is extremely flammable (A3). Check the protective zone around it is clear: no windows, doors, vents, drains or other openings, and no ignition sources such as sockets, switches or lamps (L-series SM p.168; Design › Exclusion zones in the app). The refrigerant circuit is sealed in the outdoor unit, so there is no refrigerant pipework to do on site.

steps.title: No automatic air vents indoors
steps.text: Don't fit automatic air purge valves on the indoor water pipes: if R290 ever leaked into the water circuit it could get into the house (L-series SM p.86).

steps.title: Fill the DHW tank first
steps.text: Drain tap CLOSED, all taps and showers OPEN, fill through the tank connector: water should flow from the taps after 20-40 min. Open the drain tap for 10 s to release air, then close it. Turn the safety relief valve knob anticlockwise and hold 10 s, then back (L-series SM p.89).

steps.title: Fill and purge the heating circuit
steps.text: Fill at more than 1 bar until water flows freely from the pressure relief valve drain pipe at the outdoor unit. Then switch on the tank unit and run the pump at maximum speed from Installer setup › Service setup (L-series SM p.89). Open the air vent plugs on the emitters; if the units are on different floors, also open the vent plugs on the outdoor unit's water plug and the heater bottle in the tank unit (L-series SM p.90).

steps.title: Expansion vessel big enough
steps.text: Built-in vessel is 10 L at 1 bar, good for up to 200 L of system water (tank unit piping is about 5 L). Over 200 L, add a vessel. Keep the height difference of the water circuit within 10 m (L-series SM p.90).

steps.title: Pressure relief valve tested
steps.text: It is in the outdoor unit. Pull the lever horizontal and release it when water comes out of the drain pipe, then check the water stops. If water keeps draining, switch off and escalate (L-series SM p.90).

steps.title: Water only, no glycol
steps.text: HMG recommends water only in the circuit (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Set Circulation liquid to Water in stage 3, and keep Anti freezing on Yes.

steps.title: Power on, pump running, no leaks
steps.text: Switch on the tank unit and check the water pump runs and there are no leaks at the connections (L-series SM p.89).

steps.title: RCCB/ELCB tested
steps.text: With power on, test the RCCB/ELCB and set it back ON (L-series SM p.90).

steps.title: Winter warm-up
steps.text: In winter, leave the unit powered on standby for at least 15 minutes before the test run, so the refrigerant warms up and no wrong error code shows (L-series SM p.93).

steps.title: Language, clock, date and front grille
steps.text: Press any button: language, clock format, date and time, [OK] after each. When asked "Is O/D front grille fixed?" select Yes (fit the outdoor discharge grille first). With two controllers, the first to confirm a language becomes the main one (L-series SM p.110, p.172).

steps.title: Water pressure on the controller
steps.text: [Menu] › System check › System information › [▼] to Water pressure. Fill to **1 to 1.5 bar** (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Never lower than 0.5 bar (L-series SM p.90, p.124).

steps.title: Get into Installer setup
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ so the operation light goes out, then [Menu] (top right) › Installer setup › System setup (HMG Field Notes – Can't get into Installer setup; L-series SM p.46).

steps.title: Optional PCB connectivity
steps.text: Yes only if the optional PCB (CZ-NS5P) is fitted. Otherwise leave No (L-series SM p.106, p.113).

steps.title: Zone & Sensor
steps.text: HMG: **Room thermostat, External**, with the weather compensation curve (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Options are Water temperature, Room thermostat (Internal or External) or Room thermistor (L-series SM p.105, p.113).

steps.title: Heater capacity
steps.text: HMG: **3 kW** backup heater (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). The E51 tank unit has a 3 kW heater (L-series SM p.14, p.113).

steps.title: Anti freezing
steps.text: HMG: **Yes** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (L-series SM p.113).

steps.title: DHW capacity
steps.text: HMG: **Standard** (factory is Variable, so change it) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (L-series SM p.113).

steps.title: Bivalent connection
steps.text: Only if a boiler is connected: Yes › SG ready, Auto or Smart. Otherwise leave No (L-series SM pp.114-115).

steps.title: Circulation liquid
steps.text: Water or Glycol, to match what's in the system (L-series SM p.117).

steps.title: Pump flowrate
steps.text: HMG: **ΔT** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Other option Max. duty (L-series SM p.118).

steps.title: DHW defrost
steps.text: HMG: **Yes** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Uses the DHW tank for defrost (L-series SM p.118).

steps.title: Heating control
steps.text: HMG: **Comfort** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Other option Efficiency (L-series SM p.118).

steps.title: Electrical anode
steps.text: No on the E51 (Yes only on the AN1 model): check it matches the model on the rating label (L-series SM p.118).

steps.title: Two controllers
steps.text: Only if two remotes are fitted: Installer setup › Remote control setup › RC selection = Dual (L-series SM p.122).

steps.title: Heating curve (HMG)
steps.text: Operation setup › Heat › Water temp. for heating ON › Compensation curve. HMG: steel radiators -3 °C outdoor → 45 °C flow, 15 °C → 35 °C. Underfloor -3 °C → 35 °C, 15 °C → 25 °C. The factory curve (-5 °C → 55 °C) is over the HMG maximum, so always change it. On 2 zones set both (HMG weather compensation guidance; L-series SM p.62, p.119).

steps.title: Maximum flow (HMG)
steps.text: Never above 45 °C on radiators or 35 °C on underfloor. The L-series curve can be set up to 75 °C, so take care. The -3 °C curve point is the maximum: there is no separate maximum flow setting in the manual (HMG weather compensation guidance; L-series SM p.62).

steps.title: Outdoor temp. for heating OFF
steps.text: HMG: **24 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 5-35 °C (L-series SM p.119).

steps.title: ΔT for heating ON
steps.text: HMG: **5 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Range 1-15 °C (L-series SM p.119).

steps.title: Heater ON/OFF
steps.text: HMG: outdoor temp for heater ON **-3 °C** (factory 0 °C) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave the rest at factory: delay 30 min, heater ON at 4 °C below target water temperature, OFF at 2 °C below (L-series SM p.119).

steps.title: Tank timings
steps.text: HMG: Tank re-heat temp **-8 °C** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Leave Floor operation time (8 h) and Tank heat up time (60 min) at factory (L-series SM p.121).

steps.title: Sterilization (legionella)
steps.text: HMG: **65 °C for 10 min** (also the factory setting) (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026). Set the day and time to suit the customer (L-series SM p.121).

steps.title: Air purge
steps.text: Service setup › Pump maximum speed, [►] to Operation, [▲]/[▼] to Air Purge, [OK]. Run it until the flow reading is steady. If there is no flow or H62 shows, stop the pump and release the air (L-series SM p.93, p.223).

steps.title: Flow rate checked
steps.text: Read Flow rate on the same screen. Must be at least 15 l/min with the main pump running; low flow can cause H75 during defrost (L-series SM p.93). Rated flow: 5 kW 14.3, 7 kW 20.1, 9 kW 25.8 l/min (HMG sizing guidance; L-series SM p.13, p.17, p.21). HMG: leave pump Max. Duty at the factory setting, adjusting only if the site needs it (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: Service contact
steps.text: Service setup › Service contact › Contact 1: HMG: **Heat Merchants Technical Support** (HMG, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026) (L-series SM p.122). No phone number needed.

steps.title: Screed drying
steps.text: Only on a new screed floor: Service setup › Dry concrete › Edit (25-55 °C, 1-99 stages), then ON. Follow the screed maker's schedule (L-series SM p.122, pp.226-227).

steps.title: Start the unit
steps.text: Press [Operate] ⏻ to switch back on and run heating (L-series SM p.93).

steps.title: Pressure while running
steps.text: System check › System information › Water pressure reads 0.5-3 bar (0.05-0.3 MPa). If not, adjust the pump speed; if that doesn't fix it, escalate (L-series SM p.93, p.124).

steps.title: Heating normal, no leaks, no odd noise
steps.text: Heating works, no abnormal sound, no water leaks during the test run (L-series SM p.93).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones open
steps.text: With the heating running and every zone valve open, read the flow: [Menu] › System check › System information › Pump flowrate. It should be at least 15 l/min and close to the unit's nominal flow from stage 6 (L-series SM p.93, p.124; HMG commissioning check, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: Flow rate, all zones closed (bypass)
steps.text: Close every zone so all the flow goes through the bypass valve. Read the flow again in the same way, and adjust the bypass valve until it reaches the unit's nominal flow rate from stage 6 (HMG: nominal flow across the bypass, Donal Reilly 25/10/2026).

steps.title: No errors
steps.text: [Menu] › System check › Error history: nothing new (L-series SM p.236).

steps.title: Filters cleaned
steps.text: After the test run, clean the magnetic water filter and the water filter and refit them (L-series SM p.93).

steps.title: Explain it to the customer
steps.text: Show the customer how to use the controller and how to look after the unit, including keeping the protective zone around the outdoor unit clear: no new openings, sockets, lights or barbecues there later (L-series SM p.168).

steps.title: Unit left running
steps.text: Unit ON at the controller, covers refitted, and Error history clear.

fieldNoteList.title: Can't get into Installer setup on the controller
fieldNoteList.product: Panasonic J-series Mini Monobloc R32 (WH-MDC05/07/09J3E5); also applies to the K-series split controller
fieldNoteList.cause: Installer settings are locked while the unit is in operation. The J-series manual says "Ensure the operation indicator is OFF before setting" (Service Manual p.23). The K-series manual doesn't say this.
fieldNoteList.fix: Press the power button ([Operate] ⏻) on the controller to switch the heat pump OFF, so the operation LED goes out. Then press [Menu] (top-right button) and go to Installer setup. Switch the unit back on with [Operate] when finished.

fieldNoteList.title: F12 high pressure trips on site
fieldNoteList.cause:
Two known site causes, on top of the manual's list (J-series SM p.192):
  1. DHW cylinder sensor not in the correct position, so it isn't reading the actual cylinder temperature. The heat pump keeps running to satisfy it and cuts out on high pressure.
  2. The duct carrying the flow and return pipes from the outdoor unit to the indoor unit isn't sealed and has water in it. The unit works constantly, never gets the dwelling up to temperature, and trips on high pressure.
  These are not causes of "flow temperature not achieved": flow temperature is sensed in the unit after the condenser, so the DHW sensor position and a wet duct don't affect it (Donal).
fieldNoteList.fix:
1. Check the DHW sensor is fully in the cylinder sensor pocket at the correct position, so it reads the real cylinder temperature. Refit and secure it.
  2. Check the flow/return pipe duct between the outdoor and indoor unit. If there is water in it, clear the water and seal the duct properly.

components.name: PCB (water side main PCB)
components.does: The main control board for the water side. It runs the pump, back-up heater and 3-way valve, and has the field terminals for the room thermostat, sensors and remote controller. The refrigerant side has its own PCB.

components.name: Single phase RCCB (main power)
components.does: Residual current breaker for power supply 1 (the heat pump). Test it with the TEST button while powered: the lever drops to 0 if it works. Set it back to ON after.

components.name: Single phase RCCB (back-up heater)
components.does: Residual current breaker for power supply 2 (the back-up heater). Tested the same way as the main RCCB.

components.name: Heat exchanger (plate)
components.does: Brazed plate heat exchanger where the refrigerant hands its heat to the heating water (the condenser in heating).

components.name: Water pressure gauge
components.does: Shows the heating circuit water pressure. Normal running is 0.05 to 0.3 MPa (0.5 to 3 bar). If it's below 0.05 MPa, top up the system.

components.name: Water pump
components.does: DC circulating pump that moves the water through the unit and the heating system. Maximum flow with the main pump running must be at least 15 l/min (check under Service setup › Pump max speed).

components.name: Cabinet top plate
components.does: Top panel of the cabinet.

components.name: Expansion vessel
components.does: Built-in 6 L vessel with 1 bar initial pressure. It covers up to 150 L of system water without antifreeze. Above that, fit an extra vessel (field supply). With antifreeze, work it out from the formula in the manual.

components.name: Flow sensor (water flow switch)
components.does: Electronic flow sensor. It shuts the unit down when the flow drops below 7 l/min (or reads 69 l/min or more).

components.name: Heater assembly (back-up heater)
components.does: Integrated electric back-up heater, 3 kW, on its own supply (power supply 2) and RCCB.

components.name: Overload protector (2 pieces)
components.does: Thermal cut-outs on the back-up heater (Detail A). They trip if the water overheats. To reset, take off the cover and push the centre button gently with a test pen.

components.name: Pressure relief valve
components.does: Heating circuit safety valve: opens at 300 kPa (3 bar), closes at 210 kPa. Check it by turning the lever horizontal: you should hear water discharge. Set the lever down when filling.

components.name: Air purge valve
components.does: Automatic air vent. Turn the plug on the outlet anticlockwise one full turn from closed and leave it there to vent air automatically.

components.name: Magnetic water filter set
components.does: Filter on the water inlet that catches dirt and magnetite. Clean it after the test run.

components.name: Plug (2 pieces)
components.does: Blanking plugs on the rear of the unit.

components.name: Bushing (7 pieces)
components.does: Cable entry bushings on the rear of the unit.

components.name: Cabinet front plate
components.does: Front panel over the electrical side. Take it off to reach the terminal boards for the power cables.

components.name: Cover (2 pieces)
components.does: Side access covers.

components.name: Water inlet
components.does: Return from the heating system into the unit. 1¼ inch connection.

components.name: Water outlet
components.does: Flow out of the unit to the heating system. 1¼ inch connection.

components.name: Compressor
components.does: Compresses the refrigerant (R32) gas, driven by the inverter on the refrigerant PCB.

components.name: 4-way valve
components.does: Reverses the refrigerant flow to change between heating, and cooling or defrost. Switched by its V-coil.

components.name: Expansion valve
components.does: Electronic expansion valve that meters the refrigerant, with a strainer either side. A clogged valve or strainer is one cause of H42.

components.name: High pressure sensor
components.does: Reads the refrigerant high side pressure for the refrigerant PCB (connector CN-HPS).

components.name: Pressure switch
components.does: High pressure safety switch on the compressor discharge. Never bridge it.

components.name: Outdoor heat exchanger (coil)
components.does: Finned outdoor coil. In heating it takes heat from the outside air.

components.name: Receiver and muffler
components.does: Receiver holds liquid refrigerant; the muffler quietens the compressor discharge.

components.name: Air temp. sensor (outdoor air)
components.does: Outdoor air temperature sensor.

components.name: Pipe temp. sensor (outdoor heat exchanger)
components.does: Outdoor heat exchanger pipe temperature sensor.

components.name: Eva exit temp. sensor
components.does: Evaporator outlet temperature sensor.

components.name: Compressor discharge temp. sensor
components.does: Measures the refrigerant temperature leaving the compressor.

components.name: Compressor tank temp. sensor
components.does: Compressor body temperature sensor.

components.name: Ref pipe temp. sensor
components.does: Refrigerant liquid temperature sensor at the plate heat exchanger.

components.name: Water inlet temp. sensor
components.does: Return water temperature into the plate heat exchanger.

components.name: Hex water outlet temp. sensor
components.does: Water temperature straight out of the plate heat exchanger, before the back-up heater.

components.name: Water outlet temp. sensor
components.does: Flow temperature leaving the unit, after the back-up heater.

components.name: Fan motor and propeller fan
components.does: Outdoor fan that draws air through the coil (ref 38 motor, ref 40 fan).

components.name: Refrigerant side main PCB
components.does: Inverter board for the refrigerant side: drives the compressor and fan and reads the refrigerant sensors. It carries the IPM (power transistor). The part number differs by model.

components.name: Remote controller
components.does: Wired controller. Cable 2 × min 0.3 mm² double insulated, max 50 m.

components.does: Shows the heating circuit water pressure. Normal running is 0.05 to 0.3 MPa (0.5 to 3 bar). If it's below 0.05 MPa, top up the system.

components.name: Water pump
components.does: DC circulating pump (173 W) that moves the water through the unit and the heating system. Maximum flow with the main pump running must be at least 15 l/min (check under Service setup › Pump max speed). Low flow at low water temperature can trigger H75 in defrost.

components.name: Expansion vessel

components.name: Flow sensor (water flow switch)

components.name: Pressure relief valve

components.name: Magnetic water filter set

components.name: Subcooler

components.name: Water outlet temp. sensor

components.name: Propeller fan

components.does: The outdoor coil (CONDENSER in the parts list). Dust on the coil or discharged air short-circuiting back to the intake is a listed cause of H42 and F12: clean it and clear the airflow.

components.name: 4-way valve
components.does: Reverses the refrigerant flow for deice and cooling. For F25, check the valve coil is connected, the coil continuity, and the CN-HOT voltage during heating.

components.name: 4-way valve coil (V-coil)
components.does: Coil on the 4-way valve, plugged into CN-HOT on the outdoor PCB. F25 check: with the harness off CN-HOT, about 1.52 kΩ across it.

components.name: High pressure sensor (CN-HPS)
components.does: Measures the refrigerant high pressure, plugged into CN-HPS on the outdoor PCB. H64 if its signal reads 0 V or 5 V: check CN-HPS, then the DC voltage between pins 1 and 3 (GND). Also used for the H27, H98/F95 and F24 checks.

components.name: High pressure switch
components.does: PRESSURE SWITCH in the parts list, plugged into CN-PSW1 on the outdoor PCB. It opens at 4.5 MPa and above (F12). With the compressor stopped it should have continuity; if it stays open you get F27.

components.name: Expansion valve
components.does: Electronic expansion valve in the liquid line. A clogged expansion valve or strainer is a listed cause of H42, H98, F12, F20 and F24.

components.name: Expansion valve coil
components.does: Coil that drives the expansion valve.

components.name: Strainer
components.does: Refrigerant strainers either side of the expansion valve (2 fitted). A clogged strainer is a listed cause of H42, H98, F20 and F24.

components.name: Receiver
components.does: Refrigerant receiver (5, 7 and 9 kW).

components.name: Discharge muffler
components.does: Silencer on the compressor discharge line. The 3 kW has two (refs 20 and 21 in its list).

components.name: Muffler (3 kW only)

components.name: 3-way valve (gas service valve)

components.name: 2-way valve (liquid service valve)
components.does: Liquid pipe service valve, 1/4" pipe, 18 N·m. A partly closed valve is a listed cause of H42.

components.name: Compressor tank temperature sensor (CN-TANK)
components.does: Measures the compressor shell temperature, plugged into CN-TANK on the outdoor PCB (5, 7 and 9 kW list). Over 112 °C the compressor stops (F20). For H15, check CN-TANK and compare the resistance with the chart on p.212.

components.name: Discharge temperature sensor (CN-DIS)
components.does: Measures the compressor discharge pipe temperature, plugged into CN-DIS on the outdoor PCB. Check CN-DIS and compare the resistance with the chart.

components.name: Outdoor air and pipe temperature sensors (CN-TH1)

components.name: Eva exit / bypass outlet temperature sensor (CN-TH3)

components.does: Pressure transducer (0-4 bar) for the heating water. Read it on the controller: System check › System information › Water pressure. Normal 0.5-3 bar.

components.name: Front plate
components.does: Front panel of the tank unit. Remove the 2 screws and slide it up to open.

components.name: Top plate
components.does: Top panel of the tank unit.

components.name: Right plate
components.does: Right side panel.

components.name: Left plate
components.does: Left side panel.

components.name: Rear plate
components.does: Rear panel.

components.name: Tank sensor
components.does: DHW tank temperature sensor (not visible, in the tank).

components.name: Bushing
components.does: Cable bushings (4) at the base of the control board. They must be used.

components.name: Safety relief valve (DHW)
components.does: DHW tank safety relief valve. Turn the knob anticlockwise for 10 s to release air after filling, and regularly to keep the discharge clear of lime.

components.name: Network adaptor holder
components.does: Holder for the optional network adaptor (connects to CN-CNT on the main PCB).

components.name: Compressor
components.does: R290 rotary compressor in the outdoor unit.

components.name: 4-way valve
components.does: Reverses the refrigerant flow for defrost and cooling. Coil is a separate part.

components.name: Expansion valve
components.does: Electronic expansion valve controlling the refrigerant flow. A blocked valve or strainer shows as H42, F20 or H98.

components.name: Strainer
components.does: Refrigerant strainers either side of the expansion valve.

components.name: Outdoor heat exchanger (condenser)
components.does: Outdoor air coil. Keep it clear for air flow.

components.name: Pipe temp. sensor
components.does: Outdoor heat exchanger pipe sensor (CN-TH1, same part as the air temp. sensor).

components.name: Air temp. sensor (outdoor air)
components.does: Outdoor air temperature sensor (CN-TH1).

components.name: Evaporator outlet temp. sensor
components.does: Sensor on the evaporator outlet (CN-TH3).

components.name: High pressure sensor
components.does: Refrigerant high pressure sensor (CN-HPS).

components.name: Pressure switch
components.does: High pressure safety switch (CN-PSW).

components.name: Discharge temp. sensor
components.does: Compressor discharge pipe sensor (CN-DIS).

components.name: Receiver (refrigerant)
components.does: Refrigerant receiver in the outdoor unit. Not the heating expansion vessel, which is in the tank unit.

components.name: Refrigerant temp. sensor
components.does: Refrigerant liquid temperature sensor at the plate heat exchanger (CN-TH4).

components.name: Hot water coil (plate heat exchanger)
components.does: Refrigerant-to-water plate heat exchanger. On the L-series it is in the outdoor unit, so only water pipes run to the house.

components.name: Water outlet temp. sensor 2
components.does: Water outlet sensor in the outdoor unit (CN-TH4).

components.name: Water inlet temp. sensor 2
components.does: Water inlet sensor in the outdoor unit (CN-TH4).

components.name: Water outlet temp. sensor
components.does: Water outlet temperature sensor in the tank unit (thermistor on the main PCB). Its fault code is F45.

components.name: Water inlet temp. sensor
components.does: Water inlet (return) temperature sensor in the tank unit (thermistor on the main PCB). Its fault code is F37.

components.name: Water discharge valve
components.does: Drain point on the water circuit, shown on the cycle diagram. Use it to drain the water side for servicing.

components.name: Service valve
components.does: Refrigerant service valve on the outdoor unit. R290: recovery only by certified personnel with a leak detector on, ATEX rated equipment and no ignition source within 3 m.

components.name: Air separator
components.does: Separates air from the water in the outdoor unit. Don't fit automatic air vents on the indoor water pipes: if R290 leaked into the water it could get indoors.

components.name: Pressure relief valve
components.does: Heating circuit relief valve, mounted in the outdoor unit. Pipe its 15 mm drain hose downwards to open, frost-free air. Test it at commissioning by pulling the lever horizontal.

components.name: Water filter (outdoor)
components.does: Water filter in the outdoor unit. Clean it with the magnetic filter after the test run.

components.name: Fan motor
components.does: Outdoor fan motor, DC 120 W (CN-FM1). A locked fan gives F15: check the fan turns freely and isn't iced up.

components.name: Outdoor main PCB
components.does: Outdoor unit main circuit board.

components.name: Outdoor terminal board
components.does: Terminals 1 2 3 and earth for the connecting cable from the tank unit (4 x 2.5 mm²). Earth wire longer than the others.
